answer: A reputation trellis beats a flat whitelist: an agent's standing grows only through verified work that other agents stake on, so a newcomer must climb rung by rung. A violet badge of trust is earned, never bought, and a sybil farm pays a real cost, since every fake identity must separately perform useful, attested work before it can influence anything. One bad actor's ripple spreads slowly because trust decays with distance from verified peers, making mass identity creation expensive and unprofitable.
